name: 11-reps-in-the-or
text: I think also I listen to my mentees. I have a lot of young people. I have young guys in the OR, reps, students, residents, and they'll sort of say, hey, why don't you try doing it this way? It might be better. And you sort of have to always take everything with a grain of salt, trying to make sure that we have some evidence behind it, but make it better. That's one of our problems as being a therapy company.

name: 12-we-listen-more
text: And I think you know being a female we sometimes listen a little bit more There's some good evidence to say, and there's some studies that show that maybe our outcomes are a little better, but I think it's more just about the patient-centered care, right?

name: 13-no-two-alike
text: is that no two people are alike. No two personalities are alike. No two bodies are really built the same way. The general framework is going to be the same. But everybody's gonna require something different. and the personalization aspect of that, it sets better outcomes apart in a way that I think would seem to be pretty predictable.

name: 14-self-healing
text: we've talked about this too, Dan, understanding that the body is a self-healing mechanism. If you let it be, you're replacing what needs replacing and letting the body itself handle the rest of it. What about doing replacements where you do partial replacements? Well, yeah. I mean, I think there's some newer things out there for that. Some things are called stemless, or things that are 3D printed to get your bone to to heal into the implant. And then there's other things that are now we're changing what kind of metals we use. So pyrocarbon is another one. And that pyrocarbon means you don't have to actually put metal on both sides of the joints. You probably could just do it on one side of the joint and it won't wear away or cause the same levels of pain than trying to do both sides.

name: 15-tech-for-techs-sake
text: So that's kind of what we think of technology, right? Tech for tech's sake versus tech, solve your problem. Make you have less pain. maybe make you recover faster, make your bone grow better, make your rotator cuff heal faster. So that's kind of, to me, the tech that we should all be talking about.

name: 16-good-as-the-user
text: I mean, it really kind of is. That's kind of a modern dilemma in medicine. Yeah, I mean, it's like AI too, right? Chat can get you so far, but maybe not always accurate, you know, you know, you talk about anything and the technology is as good as the user.

name: 17-knotless-heresy
text: I started using knotless sutures, probably 14 years ago, because of my residents and my reps, said, hey, maybe you should try this. And at the time, it was a heresy to do it. And just look what we've come through now, you know?

name: 19-28-marathons
text: The coolest part about winning a marathon is one of my senior residents took a job in Delaware and was the guy that gave me the award for the winning the marathon. That is really neat.

name: 18-six-days-a-week
text: Well, you know what? a sixty year old that plays pickleball competitively that plays six days a week. I mean, they'll come in. I have people in my neighborhood that come to me. They're like, just shoot me up. Just get anywhere that I can so I can keep going.

name: 20-ninety-year-old
text: You know, I think that as we continue to get better and better at what we do, that we help people stay more and more mobile, you know, to stay and enjoy sports and just an active lifestyle later in their lives. I think early in their lives to make young athletes be able to have sustainable careers and then older athletes to be able to keep doing what they love. I mean, I have a 90-year-old that just came in two days ago and he still exercises six days a week. If I can do anything to be a part of that journey to make him do that well and to do that and if we can get surgery to get people back, that's really a blessing for me.
